raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Dog Food
raw_recipe.description: This homemade dog food can be fed to dogs on its own or mixed in with kibble. Made with turkey, rice, and veggies — it’s sure to make some tails wag!

video.description: Sometimes, your pets need a little recipe love too. In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to make homemade dog food for your beloved furry friends! Made with a combination of ground turkey and brown rice, this is guaranteed to be a delicious treat for any dog.

review.reviewBody: I think this is a great basic recipe to add to. I ususally double this recipe and make the following changes. First I vary the meat each week, sometimes turkey, chicken, beef and occasionally some liver added. I used 2 1/2 pounds of meat which is just a little more than the recipe calls for, but I also add 6 beaten eggs which I whirl into the boiling mix as it cooks. I think variety is very important so I also change grains with each week. I have used lentils, barley, brown rice or even oatmeal. Make sure your garlic is cooked as raw garlic can make your dog sick, and never use onions as a vegetable as onions make them sick as well. I use a variety of vegetables and mix and match them in each batch. I don't use the gassy veggies like brocoli or cauliflower as my guys have tender tummies and all the gas just wouldn't be good. I do use a mix of fresh and frozen veggies usually carrots, peas, green beans and squash. It is very important to cook your grains well and also to whirl the veggies up in the blender since dogs have short intestinal tracks and can not digest these carbohydrates easily and won't get the nutrition that they need from them if they are left whole. Make sure they get their calcium! I save all my egg shells and rinse them out. I bake them for 10 minutes in a 300 degree oven to get them nice and brittle, then blend them until they are powder. I put a spoon of eggshell powder and a spoon of Omega supplement on each feeding.

This is not a bad basic recipe, but there are a few things not addressed. I have been making my own pet foods for several years now, and while the protein to carbohydrate ratio in this is not bad, there are no organ meats to provide added essential nutrients (I would throw in a couple of chicken hearts and livers), there is no calcium source (a couple of tums with calcium would do), and no table salt to add iodine. Also, dogs do not chew as humans do, and their bodies will not break down vegetable matter as well as ours can, so all vegetables should be well pureed so that your dog can get the maximum nutritional value from it. It should also be noted that while many well cooked, pureed veggies are fine for your dog, onions, raisins, garlic, grapes, and even tomatoes should be avoided, because they contain naturally occurring ingredients that can cause various health problems in your pet. I would also prefer to see a little more fat in this recipe for a normal weight dog, their bodies need more fat than ours do. My dog is on a 35% meat, 15% fat, 40% grain (always rice, corn and wheat are allergens) and about 10% vegetable matter diet, and he does very well. This recipe is good in principle, it just needs a few things added :)

I think this is a great recipe. But I have a tip. If you own a pressure cooker you can take the chicken bones that the meat was deboned from and cook for about 45 minutes to 60 minutes in the pressure cooker with the broth water from the chicken you cooked until you can crush between you fingers. The bones will be really soft and put in blender and blend into a liquid. This way you get all the marrow and the calcium. Mix some of it in the dog food . gives great flavor too.

good basic recipe but I would omit the cauliflower and broccoli. causes horrible gastric upset in dogs (as in gas). I cook fresh ground turkey, add brown rice, cooked chopped carrots and a 1 TBS of plain yogurt and 2 TBS of cottage cheese. My vet told me that cottage cheese and yogurt are great for dogs with upset stomachs. Also adding a touch of canned plain pumpkin (not the kind with spices) to their diet is very good too. Canned pumpkin also helps with constipation!

I just started making my Rat Terrier his dog food and he's been healthy ever since. I put a couple boneless chicken breasts, a lb of baby carrots in a slow cooker w/ a lot of water and cook all day. The last hour I add frozen green peas and brown and white rice. (No seasonings, herbs, or spices). When it's done it's like Chicken Stew. I freeze individual servings and remove from freezer daily. My dog loves it. It's easy for me too.

I did not use ground turkey instead I bought Chicken leg quarters (5 LBS) and cut the metl off the bones and boiled meat for an hour.. high and then low temp. Then I boiled frozen green beans, carrots, peas, broccoli, cauliflower, squash, sweet potatoes and boiled and then ran through the blender. I then cooked brown rice in 4 cups chicken boil water and 2 cups rice in the water that I boiled the chicken in pots. I then boil one dozen eggs and put in blender with a little bonebroth to make smooth. I then mix 1/2 chicken and 1/2 rice with vegetables and eggs divided between zip lock bags. It makes about a week of food for my 45lb Springer, 14lb dachshund and 6lb Chihuahua. I add vitamin and mineral powder from Chewy. I put just a little dry kibble in the bottom of the bowl for crunch, 1 raw chicken bone to large dog bowl and divide between dogs according to size. They LOVE it and it is less expensive than frozen or refrigerator dog foo. I freeze 4 days and leave 3 in frig and each day bring one out from freezer so in 2 days it thaws in the frig.

I’ve fed raw for 30 years but wanted to make a change with my new puppy. This is a great base recipe but I’ve made a few changes. I buy fresh vegetables which cuts down on the salt from processed foods and after cooking them I purée them since a dog’s short intestinal tract isn’t made to break down the cellulose layer of vegetables allowing them to absorb the nutrients. I lower the water a bit to allow for puréed vegetation. I change up the proteins and vegetables also switching up brown rice, barley, and oatmeal. I also like to purchase boneless skinless chicken and after cooking shred it. Cooking up a 10 pound bag of chicken leg quarters (I rinse the leg quarters a lot because of the brine/salt they add unless I’m able to purchase fresh chicken) and reducing the bones into a bone broth adds a nice extra for the pup too. I choose to cook up a few large batches and freeze them in daily sized freezer containers. It’s easier on me physically because I never know if my health issues will interfere with cooking up a batch of food, this way I’ve always got food ready to go. I’m still working on the portions I want to feed since my pup is still on three meals per day. I do envy the people who own little chihuahuas etc., having a large breed dog the recipe doesn’t last as long as it would with a smaller breed.

Thank you for this. I cooked a diced sweet potato along with the rice, rosemary, and turkey, boiled and then simmered for 25 mins. I then added frozen peas and a couple of beaten eggs. Simmered for an additional 5 mins. and it was perfect. I generally mix it with dried food as I think my dog needs that for her teeth! She loves this homemade food though!

Good recipe. I generally add 1 tsp olive oil per serving when feeding. Also add multivitamin and raw egg every other day. PLEASE NOTE: Previous review stated they gave their dogs raw chicken bones. DO NOT DO THIS...Unless you want a hefty vet bill or potentially your loved one put down when you can't afford the surgery. Chicken bones are NOT ok to give your dog! Chicken bones splinter, are very sharp and very likely to cause internal issues. Do a google search before you give your dog a chicken bone please.

It is a really good base. I read through the comments and took the advice from some of the other doggy parents and added some extras. I bought the Normandy blend frozen veggies from Bird’s Eye and steamed a half a bag of those along with a few handfuls of collard greens and then pulsed them through the food processor until they were mostly in tiny bits, but not mushy. I used the water from the steamed veggies to make up part of the water I used to cook the rice. Then I added the veggies, a can of purée pumpkin, and a can of no salt added spinach. I added shredded sweet potato and let it soften at the end of steaming my veggies. I also minced some chicken livers because they are supposed to be very healthy as well. My doggy loved it! And I feel like with all of that, along with a chewable supplement for dogs he will get all the nutrients he needs

This was a huge hit with my dog Oliver who’s a very picky eater. My only “issue” is that there was so much excess water left over when it was done cooking so I had to drain that before serving it to my dog. I’m not sure if I missed a step or did something wrong but next time, I’ll just use less water. Maybe 3-4 cups instead of 6. This time I went with a corn/peas/carrots/green beans option but Ollie wasn’t too keen on peas or corn. I also added in a little sweet potato which he loved. I’m excited to try this again with different meat and veggie combos for him in the future.
Great basic recipe. Enough for 2 meals for my 220 pound mastiff. I generally just top his kibble, small meals 2-3 times daily to avoid bloat. No broccoli
My homemade dog food is similar but I add coconut oil, flaxseed, and egg shells for calcium and essential fatty acids.
Love it
I make this for my pups and it's their early evening meal. Kibble in the morning, this in the evening. Their favorite added veggies are carrots, peas and broccoli. They love it.
